sentences.text: The title block is the first thing to read on any chart.

It gives the chart number, title and scale; the units for soundings, which may be feet, fathoms or meters; the vertical datum for depths, usually mean lower low water; and the horizontal datum, normally the North American Datum of 1983, which for practical purposes matches the WGS 84 datum your GPS uses.
If your plotter and chart use different datums, positions can be off.
Heights of lights and landmarks and bridge clearances are measured above mean high water.
Check the edition date too, and keep the chart corrected.
NOAA is moving from traditional paper charts to electronic charts, so check what’s currently available for your area.
